theme: Building a structure by letting it build itself
title: Self-Assembly Scheduling: Outrunning the Kinetic Trap
innovation_hook: Forming the strongest bonds first maximizes early yield and locks the system in a kinetic trap that cannot rearrange into the target; the insight is to deliberately schedule weak, reversible bonds first so errors can anneal out, holding the strong (decoy) bonds back until the target has already frozen into place.
strategies: trivial: reproduce the checker's own reference construction -- enable every bond simultaneously at one fixed late step, regardless of type or strength (-> ~0.1)

greedy: enable bonds strictly in decreasing strength order (strongest/decoys first) -- looks like it maximizes early yield, but permanently freezes decoys onto monomers the target needs before the (weaker) target bonds ever get a turn
strong: enable every target bond at step 1 and hold every decoy back to the very last step, so target bonds anneal into the correct configuration while decoys arrive too late to ever bind
